newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO appeals for $14.3 million North Korea food aid.
newsitem.headline: FAO appeals for $14.3 million North Korea food aid.

text.p: The U.N.'s Food and Agricultural Organisation appealed on Monday for $14.3 million in food aid for famine-threatened North Korea.

"FAO is appealing to the international community to fund six projects for a total value of $14.3 million to help (North Korea) restore its ability to produce sufficient quantities of food," the Rome-based agency said in a statement.
It added that North Korea was suffering a severe food shortage caused by three years of poor agricultural production following unprecedented flooding in 1995-96.

"People are suffering from food shortage and since early March 1997, food rations have been reduced to 100 grammes of rice a day against a normal ration of 500 grammes," FAO consultant Jan Driessen, who has just returned from North Korea, said in the statement.

FAO said the planned projects were aimed at restoring normal agricultural yields in North Korea and ranged from repairing flood-damaged irrigation systems to implementing double cropping techniques in order to improve cereal harvests.

The World Food Programme, the main body involved in getting supplies into North Korea, said last week the country was still on the verge of famine and that donations so far of $34 million would not meet its needs.
North Korean officials have tied progress in four-nation peace negotiations with South Korea, China and the United States to substantial international assistance.
Seoul and Washington maintain that new large-scale aid can not be discussed until Pyongyang responds conclusively to a proposal for further peace talks.
